text:
## R-01 A kit, not a system

Squiddy is a library, a skill and templates that each graph instantiates locally. It never stores
content and never runs as a service. Evidence: Wintermute's monolith drift, diagnosed by the
operator on 2026-09-10 as "ingest machinery centralized while the design said distributed, so
content followed the only pipeline that existed" (DI-004). Prior art: OBO Foundry ODK and ROBOT
(Jackson et al. 2019; Matentzoglu et al. 2022), Monarch's LinkML/KGX/Koza/KG-Hub stack, Seldon
AD-002 (domain-agnostic engine, domain configuration as schema).

## R-02 Extract, do not design

The kit's first version is `icsp_notebook`'s `kg/admit.py` spine with FSS-specific parts factored
to configuration. Rule of three satisfied (fss-policy-kg, AI-readiness KG, Wintermute, and
ai-readiness-kg as the fourth per S-001). Measured by S-001: 88% of stages and 94% of spine lines
generic or parameterizable. Failure mode avoided: Brooks's second-system effect.

## R-03 No rewrite to RDF/OWL

Property graph and JSONL ledger stay. LinkML is the schema language on top; ontology identifiers
are referenced by CURIE, never copied. Evidence: the biomedical graphs the operator half-recalled
as "the OWL paradigm" are property graphs on Neo4j with formal schemas (Hetionet, Himmelstein et
al. 2017; SPOKE, Morris et al. 2023; Biolink, Unni et al. 2022; BioCypher, Lobentanzer et al.
2023). The OWL lives in the vocabularies, not the store.

## R-04 The invariant is mandated; the store is not

Every assertion immutable and provenanced; every derived state reproducible from primary sources
plus the recorded process; one write path emitting an event; a write that bypasses it is the one
forbidden act. Which store is called "truth" is declared per graph: fss-policy-kg is
ledger-as-truth (its served product is a NetworkX projection with no Neo4j); an Arnold graph may be
graph-as-truth. Both conform. Evidence: W3C PROV-O; nanopublications (Groth, Gibson, Velterop
2010); NASA EOSDIS data levels; FAIR (Wilkinson et al. 2016). This closes the Arnold thread's
"reverse the JSONL ruling" question: it is not a reversal, it is a declaration.

## R-05 Candidate kits: measure before adopting

Pre-registered rule (adopt / harvest components / reject), applied in S-001. Result: no candidate
passes adopt; LinkML adopted for schema, KGX for interchange, BioCypher / Koza / ODK / ROBOT harvest
components, TrustGraph and Neo4j LLM Graph Builder rejected (TrustGraph's components already
harvested 2026-08-23 in ai-readiness-kg). The BioCypher spike is not triggered.

## R-06 LinkML ratified at corrected scope

S-003 measured: the "1,565-line dual projection" was two files, not the duplication. Removable
with the schema: 489 of 821 projection lines (60%). Not removable by any schema: the
event-to-instance transform (217 lines, written once, Koza's layer) and store semantics (115
lines). The parity gate becomes two writers over one instance stream plus schema validation at
export, because two LinkML generators disagreed on one slot in the same run.

## R-07 First consumer is the bibliographic evidence graph; Arnold is second

Bounded to what the kit's recorded decisions cite plus the standards they rest on; public
metadata, abstracts, open-access text only; DOI and OpenAlex as its identity spine. Reasons: entity
resolution nearly solved by external authorities; abundant schema prior art (CiTO, FaBiO, schema.org
ScholarlyArticle); it eats its own dog food. Arnold's domain (clinical vocabularies, a person as an
entity, wearable time series) is the hardest kind and should meet a kit already proven. This
disagrees with the Arnold thread's proposal and is the ruling.

## R-08 The manifest is the inventory control system for every graph

One entry per document ever considered (cataloged, held, admitted, declined with reason and
metadata); nothing enters a graph except through it; manifest-vs-graph disagreement is a gate
failure. Public-only is a per-graph policy the manifest declares and the assessment stage
enforces. Inherited from fss-policy-kg's 2026-09-10 rule (DI-070, DI-071).

## R-09 Identity spine: local mint, registry election, bridge by record (OD-4 defaults stand)

S-004's five assumptions accepted without an override window, per the doctrine (decide, state,
proceed): A1 the registry elects an existing id and mints nothing; A2 it is a zero-content Squiddy
graph beside seldon-ontology, not inside it; A3 `exactMatch` only on declared authority key
equality or a human ruling, everything probabilistic is `closeMatch` and non-transitive (SKOS
Reference 2009); A4 query-time lookup serves recorded bridges and decides nothing (Translator
NodeNorm); A5 the Work is the unit, DOIs identify expressions (FRBR; DI-152). Evidence and prior
art in `docs/OD-4_identity_spine.md` §7 (31 sources). The operator overrides by naming the letter.

## R-10 Maintenance is scheduled stages with gates, never unbounded agents

Currency, drift, dedup, and the measure-before-commit re-extraction loop (parked design in
icsp_notebook) run as scheduled pipeline stages. The weekly sweep is the template; Wintermute's
OODA self-healer is the counterexample.

## R-11 Secrets and API keys

Credentials live in `.env` at the repo root, gitignored, with a committed `.env.example` naming
every variable and none of the values. The kit's acquire stage reads `OPENALEX_API_KEY` (and any
other authority credential) from the environment through one accessor, never from config files,
never logged, never written into a manifest, a report, or an event. Absent a key, the stage runs
in the public pool and records `auth: none` on the run. The operator has an OpenAlex key and adds
it to `.env` himself; no task asks for it, prints it, or moves it.

## R-12 Budget is never a target

Unused weekly quota is not spent on extraction ahead of a manifest, a schema, or a pipeline. The
first consumer reaches the acceptance bar with zero model calls by design (its first assertions
are deterministic from public sources).

## R-13 After the ask is met, stop

Recorded because it was violated on icsp_notebook on 2026-09-10 (arcs dispatched by mining
delivery reports). Findings about other repos discovered by kit work (S-003's three fss-policy-kg
defects) are reported to the operator, not dispatched.

## R-14 Extraction: grounded by the harness, stamped, shown before commit, pilot before bulk

The kit's extraction stage is the generic half of fss-policy-kg's E3 under the Max OAuth client
policy (D34, `kg/models.yaml`), with the grounding span located and verified by the harness rather
than quoted by the model (ai-readiness-kg's contract, S-001 finding 2), an extractor stamp carrying
the resolved version (DI-023), assertions written to evidence and rendered by the preview stage
before the write path admits them (OD-5 made real), and a pre-registered pilot gate with a
positive control before any bulk run (DI-030; the G4 ruling that any graph attempt carries its own
gate). Token usage captured from the CLI envelope on run one. First proving ground: claims from
the bibliographic graph's open-access texts, because extraction is the critical path to the second
consumer and the bibliographic graph is where a failure costs least.

## R-15 Four things, one truth

A Squiddy graph is four things. Only one of them is the record.

| # | thing | what it is | lifetime | in git | how it is made |
|--:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Ledger** `events.jsonl` | Append-only, immutable event log. Every assertion, retraction, ruling and admission, in order, with provenance. **The source of truth and the audit record.** | Permanent | Yes, tracked (DI-001; the icsp gitignore says why: E3 events are stochastic and not regenerable) | The single write path appends; nothing else touches it (DI-010) |
| 2 | **NetworkX projection** | In-memory graph rebuilt from the ledger by reset-then-replay (about one second on fss-policy-kg). Runs the gates, the drift check, the export and the parity check without a live driver (DI-007). | One process | No; it is never written to disk as itself | Replay of #1 |
| 3 | **Neo4j database** | The live projection you query, explore and serve MCP verbs from. One database per graph, database name = graph name (DI-004, DI-005). | Long-lived but disposable: reset-then-replay from #1 reproduces it exactly, and the drift check proves it (DI-040) | No | Replay of #1 |
| 4 | **Export** (node-link JSON, versioned) | Release artifact: portable copy, deployment copy where Neo4j is unavailable (the HF Space), input to the release diff. One row per version in the register (DI-110). | Kept on disk per the register; regenerable | No (35 MB per copy on fss-policy-kg; churn) | Written from #2 |

Ledger-as-truth is the ruling for every graph Squiddy builds. R-04 left "which store is truth" per
graph; this note closes that for Squiddy graphs. Reason: Neo4j writes are `MERGE` and `SET n +=`,
which overwrite; an overwritten value leaves no record of what it replaced. The audit evidence
State Fidelity Validity requires (an immutable record plus the recorded process that reproduces
every derived state) can only be the ledger. Neo4j is where you work; the ledger is what you can
prove. A write to Neo4j that did not go through the ledger vanishes on the next rebuild and is a
drift-check failure, not a feature (DI-011).

## R-16 The ledger is segmented, because the record is the thing that grows

Measured 2026-09-13: `icsp_notebook/kg/events.jsonl` is 64,273,858 bytes, tracked in git. GitHub
warns at 50 MB and refuses at 100 MB. fss-policy-kg is already past the warning.

Prior art: every event-sourced store segments its log (Kafka log segments; EventStoreDB chunk
files; Fowler's Event Sourcing pattern with snapshots). The kit's form: one immutable ledger file
per release (`ledger/<release>.jsonl`), sealed when the release is cut, plus an index file naming
the segments in order and each one's sha256. Replay reads the segments in index order. A sealed
segment is never appended to. No single file grows past a bound, git diffs are per release, and a
segment's hash in the register is its integrity check. Git LFS is rejected: pointers break plain
`git diff` and every clone has to fetch blobs it may never replay.

Whether the kit already writes under the release marker in a way that makes this a rename or a
change is measured in S-009 before anything is written; the FSS ledger is not touched (locked for
the deliverable).

## R-17 TEVV is the gate structure, not a phase

Test, evaluation, verification and validation (NIST AI RMF vocabulary) are already what the kit's
gates do; this ruling names the requirements so nothing is added later "because we should have".

| id | requirement | inherited from |
|---|---|---|
| T-1 | Every model-touching stage runs behind a pre-registered pilot gate whose thresholds are checked for reachability before registration (Wilson bound, sample sized to the threshold). | DI-030, DI-034; S-007's rater line is the recorded miss |
| T-2 | Every gate instrument is positive-controlled and mutation-tested before its verdict enters a decision; the decision names the instrument version and the control run. | DI-099, DI-100; S-007 §6.1 is the demonstration |
| T-3 | Every quantitative statement about a graph is a registered Result with its evidence file. | DI-042, DI-095 |
| T-4 | Every release passes the drift check (manifest = ledger = served export) and the parity gate where two projections exist. | DI-040, DI-002 |
| T-5 | Density gate: relationship types non-empty; edges per node above a floor; orphan share below a ceiling; every Claim reachable from a Concept and a Decision. Values are the graph's, pre-registered. | G4 record (DI-035 to DI-039) |
| T-6 | The SFV reproducibility indicators (DI-102) are emitted per release, as control signals with tolerance bands, never a composite score. | sfv-paper §7 |
| T-7 | Every maintenance job names the consumer of its output before it is scheduled. | DI-136 |
| T-8 | Every Squiddy graph is a data product measured by the existing AI readiness instrument (`ai-readiness-kg/framework/ai_readiness_framework.json`, 48 indicators, 7 criteria): its served surface is admitted to the scan frame as an internal cohort, never mixed into the FSS findings; the public-tier AUTO indicators run through the existing harness; the release stage emits a readiness manifest carrying the agency_instrumented evidence the kit already produces (A7, B2, B5, D3, E2, E3, E5, F1, F6, G4). No new indicators are defined here. | ai-readiness-kg, scan cycle 2026-09-07 |

## R-18 Continuous improvement is a scheduled, bounded, receipted stage

The operator's intent: when there is capacity, sample a hundred claims, correct what fails spec,
record who reviewed each and what changed, and the graph is a hundred claims better.

The form that intent takes is fixed by R-10 and R-12. "We have spare cycles, go improve the graph"
is the trigger that produced Wintermute's self-healer (DI-137) and the R-13 violation on
icsp_notebook; it is refused as a trigger. The same work as a stage is correct:

- **Audit sweep stage.** Sample n claims by sha256 order of claim id (the S-007 rule), n fixed in
  the graph's config, rated against the fixed rubric; every verdict a `Ruling` node with
  `RulesOn`; corrections written as retract-and-append events, never edits (DI-013, DI-053).
  Registers per run: claims sampled, share failing, share corrected, tokens. Scheduled on a
  cadence (the weekly sweep template), never by capacity.
- **Reviewer provenance.** The `Ruling` schema gains `agent_kind: model | human` and `agent`: the
  resolved model id (DI-023) or the human's name. A human review is a ruling like any other;
  it is never a gate (DI-098). The audit sweep's consumer (T-7) is the served `status` on each
  claim, which every verb already returns.
- **Re-extraction loop.** When a prompt, model or segment rule changes, the measure-before-commit
  loop (DI-026): fixed stratified sample, model-rater gold set with adjudication, commit rule
  "B replaces A for future admissions only if the rater line improves without grounding falling",
  installed base re-extracted per document as logged retire-and-replace.
- **Cross-graph dedup and currency** are stages of the same shape, scheduled, gated, receipted.

## R-19 Design before build, because the ledger is append-only

The operator asked for the waterfall shape: high agreement on the first stage and the best
available picture of the later ones before any build. Royce (1970), whom the word is credited to,
argued the single pass fails and drew the feedback loops; what has changed is the cost of a loop,
not the cost of a design error. In this system a design error is the expensive kind: schema and
invariant mistakes propagate into an immutable ledger and are corrected by logged retraction, not
erased. So the front-loaded stage is schema, invariants, gates and vocabulary; everything
stochastic runs behind a pilot; and the feedback loop is the pre-registered gate that fails, which
is cheap because it was designed to be. Agreement on the plan is recorded as the proposed tasks
below; a build thread executes them and does not redesign them.

## R-20 The prefix is everything in the call that is not segment or output

H-004's parent file defines the fixed prefix as "instruction plus schema". Two registered results
contradict that reading. HV-008 finding 2: 5,340 mean metered tokens per extractor call, about 490
of it the paper text and the prompt together, the rest CLI per-call scaffolding and side models.
S-007 pilot: 1,327 input tokens per invocation to a Haiku side call the CLI makes itself. The
instruction is therefore the small part, and a task that measured only it would confirm a
breakdown nobody disputes while leaving the 5k unexplained. Part A reports the call by component
(CLI default system prompt, built-in tool definitions, MCP tool definitions, memory injection,
environment block, instruction plus schema, segment, output, side calls), each registered.

Consequence: H-004 Part C (a shorter instruction) is skipped by its own 2,000-token condition when
that condition is read against the instruction's row. Halving 490 tokens cannot move a 5k prefix.

## R-21 A fourth remedy: minimal-scaffold invocation, compared under the same rules

Remedy 1 converts prefix creation into prefix reads. Removing the prefix is the other half of the
design space and H-004 did not list it. Prior art: `takelushi/claude-code-rs` (tested against CLI
v2.1.94) ships it as the default configuration, stated purpose "to reduce unnecessary context sent
to the CLI": no session persistence, empty setting sources, strict and empty MCP config, no
built-in tools, no slash commands, the caller's text as the entire system prompt. Anthropic's CLI
reference documents `--system-prompt` as replacing the default prompt and a `--bare` mode. Same
client and same auth, so R-11 holds. Flags are verified against the installed CLI's help, never
recalled.

It is compared, not adopted: it changes what the model sees, so claims ratio (at or above 0.85 of
baseline) and per-paper grounding (at or above 0.95) are real tests, exactly as for H-002's
batching, which saved 6.7x and was refused. It runs before Remedy 1 because a prefix diff is
cheaper on a small prefix and because prompt caching has a model-specific minimum cacheable
length: below it Remedy 1 has nothing to act on and the two do not combine.

## R-22 The daemon pauses while the arms run

One rate limit, one prompt-cache namespace, one ledger. A cache-read share measured while a second
process issues near-identical prefixes is contaminated in the direction of the hypothesis under
test. And the 100M ceiling does not refund tokens spent at the baseline rate while a cheaper
transport is hours from a verdict: at 600k per hour against a baseline projection near 330M, the
ceiling already buys under a third of the corpus. Pause through the daemon's own `write_pause`,
resume in H-004 Part E under whatever passed, or under the unchanged baseline if nothing did.

## R-23 The SessionStart hook is unrecorded process, which the invariant forbids

H-004 found a user-level `SessionStart` hook injecting a 2,799-token skills preamble into all 3,235
extraction calls. CLAUDE.md's invariant: every derived state reproducible from primary sources plus
the recorded process. Text from `~/.claude` that reaches the extractor and appears in no record is
process that was not recorded. A re-run on another machine, or on this one after the hook changes,
is a different extractor under the same version string. So `--setting-sources ""` is owed on
reproducibility grounds whatever the cost comparison says, and the existing claims need the hook's
text hashed and attached to their runs by an appended event while that text is still recoverable.

This does NOT adopt Remedy 4. The per-paper grounding floor refused it and that verdict stays on
the record. R-23 says why the question must be re-asked properly, and R-24 says how.

## R-24 A refused arm is re-tested on unseen papers against a threshold that predates every arm

Rules 12.3's floor (0.95 per paper, not pooled) has no noise term. `findings_acl_972` sits at
exactly 0.9500 in the baseline, so a second baseline run would fail its own floor on roughly half
of attempts; the rule cannot tell an arm from a replicate on that paper. Prior art: non-inferiority
designs state a margin and a confidence bound before the data (Piaggio et al. 2012, CONSORT
extension; FDA 2016 guidance); A/A runs measure what a comparison calls a difference when none
exists (Kohavi, Tang and Xu 2020, ch. 19); Newcombe 1998 for the interval on a difference of
proportions. S-012 already carries the same defect for the rater gate (Wilson bound).

The frame, fixed here before any call:
- Verdict papers: the 15 pilot papers no remedy arm has touched. The five H-002 papers are reported
  beside them and excluded from the verdict, because they are the data that prompted this ruling.
- Lines: the daemon's own pilot gate, in config since S-007 and older than every arm. Pooled
  grounding at or above 0.98; schema validity at or above 0.98; GROUNDED claims at or above 0.85 of
  the baseline's grounded claims on the same 15 (ungrounded claims never reach the ledger, so yield
  of grounded claims is the quantity that matters). Newcombe 95 percent interval on the grounding
  difference reported, not gated.
- Noise: one replicate of the arm on the five seen papers, giving an A/A pair per paper. Reported.

The objection is DI-174's and is recorded rather than answered away: this frame was written after
seeing an arm fail the old one. What separates it from a moved threshold is that the verdict rests
on papers no arm has seen and on lines nobody chose for this comparison.

## R-25 Transport-only changes are probed first because they cannot change a claim

Three candidates change what the CLI does around the extractor and nothing the extractor reads:
the side-model calls (1,378 tokens, 51 percent of a minimal call; `DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS`
and `--bare` are the documented candidates), prompt-cache writes that are never read
(`DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING`; H-004 notes the writes are the 1-hour kind, priced at 2x, against a
read share of zero), and whatever else `claude --help` and code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars list
for headless use. Each is a three-call probe. Any that works joins the arm R-24 tests.

## R-26 Under a ceiling that buys a fraction of the corpus, order is the design

Papers 21 and 22 are about a million characters each and cost 9 to 13M tokens apiece; 69M remaining
buys five to seven such documents, or several hundred ordinary ones. With a fixed budget and
unequal costs this is the knapsack problem, and the standard heuristic is greedy by value per unit
cost (Dantzig 1957; within a factor of two of optimal once the single best item is also considered). The value measure this graph already holds: citation
events per work in the operator's own threads. Order = citation events divided by estimated
tokens, descending. No size cap: a heavily cited long work still earns its place by the ratio.

## R-27 The cost gate checks every completed paper

H-004 scoped the gate to the pilot's twenty and the first paper past them scored 37.06 against 35,
unseen. Removing the scope restriction is not choosing a window: the bound already says worst
paper. After any adoption the bound is re-derived by H-004's own formula (1.25 times structural)
from the adopted call cost, before the daemon resumes.

## R-28 Value is concept coverage with diminishing returns, because the citation layer cannot rank

R-26 ordered by citation events per token. H-005 found every work carries the same citation value,
so the ratio collapsed to shortest-first: a rule nobody chose, which buys the 535 shortest works
and leaves the 293 longest unread. The mention layer HV-009 released gives each work a concept set
before any model call (15,219 edges, 4,167 concepts). With a budget and sets, this is budgeted
maximum coverage (Khuller, Moss and Naor 1999); DN-005's first draft named it and was wrong to
retreat to the knapsack reading.

Plain coverage pays only for the first work on a concept, and S-013 needs the opposite: two claims
from different works on one concept before a contradiction candidate can exist. So the value of
adding a work is the sum over its concepts of 1/(k+1), k being the works already chosen that cover
that concept. That function is monotone submodular; greedy by marginal value per token holds a
constant-factor guarantee under a knapsack constraint (Nemhauser, Wolsey and Fisher 1978;
Sviridenko 2004). Recomputed at each paper boundary, zero model calls. First, measure why the
citation layer is flat (its distribution), because a flat value layer is either a fact about the
corpus or a defect in the citation parse, and the second is Issue 8e888b61's open condition (3).

## R-29 The cost gate watches tokens per call, on a control chart, at every paper

The multiple (tokens spent over the paper's own text tokens) moves with mean segment length, a
property of the paper. Paper 21 scored 1.32 times structural on short segments alone; the bound is
1.25 times. Shortest-first now feeds the daemon exactly the documents most likely to have short
segments, so the gate as written will refuse the protocol for something the protocol did not do,
at the next daemon start, and H-005 notes it is decided once. What a cost gate exists to catch is
the fixed part of a call growing: a hook, a CLI release that adds scaffolding, a side call coming
back. That is tokens per call net of segment and answer, and the instrument for a process mean
with known spread is a Shewhart chart with 3-sigma limits on the per-paper mean (Montgomery,
Introduction to Statistical Quality Control, ch. 6). Limits from H-005's 2,876 adopted calls,
written before the next paper. Checked at every paper boundary; out of limits pauses the daemon
with a named reason. The multiple stays as a reported number.

## R-30 The CLI version is part of the extractor and goes in every record

The binary upgraded 2.1.274 to 2.1.275 mid-verdict and no record says which extracted what. R-23
applied to the one component that changes with nobody acting. Every record stamps the version the
call ran under. The daemon resolves the binary by a pinned version path, not the moving symlink, if
the install layout allows it; a version change then becomes a config edit and a new pilot, which is
what a changed extractor is owed. The adopted variable is documented as implying
`DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`, so the upgrade likely came from an interactive session sharing the install;
hypothesis, to be checked against the install log. The two-version split inside H-005's 15 is
backfilled from record timestamps against the new binary's install time, by appended event.

## R-31 The adopted arm returns 8.7 percent fewer grounded claims, and that is signal

H-005's A/A pair moved claim counts by at most one per paper. 1,211 against 1,326 is therefore an
instrument effect, inside the pre-registered 0.85 line and correctly adopted. What the removed
preamble was eliciting is unknown. Characterize the difference on the 15 paired papers with zero
model calls: by section, by claim type, by segment length, and whether the missing claims cluster
in few papers. If they are a kind the graph wants, the remedy is the instruction, under its own
pre-registered comparison, not the scaffold.

## R-32 The control chart of R-29 is withdrawn; the threat it watched is now closed by construction

H-006 built the chart to DN-006's specification and it failed its negative control: 54 of 288
papers signal, paper 21's profile among them. The specification was wrong in two places, both
Desktop's. Limits of 3 sigma over root n treat calls as exchangeable across papers, and they are
not: the variation between papers dwarfs the variation within one, the case the three-way chart
exists for (Wheeler, Understanding Statistical Process Control, ch. 9; Montgomery section 6.4 on
rational subgroups). And the statistic subtracted segment tokens estimated at one corpus-wide 2.98
characters per token, so each paper's own tokenization ratio landed in the "fixed" residual. CC
refused to install it, correctly.

It is not rebuilt. What it was for was the fixed part of a call growing unseen. Since H-005 and
H-006 that part can change only through a config edit: setting sources are off and checked by the
stage, the binary is pinned and verified at start, and a new version is a new pilot. A detective
control over something preventive controls already hold is cost without a threat. The per-paper
intercept of presented tokens on segment characters (the fixed cost with the paper's own
tokenization taken out) is logged as a number on each paper and gates nothing. `chart.enabled`
stays false and the block says why.

## R-33 Find what restarts the daemon, and checkpoint by segment before the long documents arrive

daemon.log shows a new run id at 09:53:53Z and 10:46:40Z on 2026-09-20, each about 40 seconds into
a paper, 53 minutes apart. Cause unknown; hypotheses, none asserted: a crash on those papers' first
calls with launchd restarting, a periodic external job, another session. A paper persists nothing
until it completes (H-005 lost 1.79M to that). Four documents over 500,000 characters remain and
each needs roughly an hour of wall time at the present pace. If restarts recur at under an hour,
those documents cannot finish and each attempt burns its tokens. DN-006 left checkpointing unruled
at a bounded loss; an unbounded one changes that. Per-segment records, written through the same
path, resumed by segment id on restart, with T-2's planted control: kill mid-paper, restart, no
segment called twice, claims identical to an uninterrupted run's set for the segments already done.

## R-34 Test-retest reliability of the extractor is measured before anything downstream leans on claim identity

H-005's A/A pair moved claim COUNTS by at most one per paper. H-006 Part D then found 330 of 1,326
baseline claims with no overlapping candidate claim in the same segment, 215 candidate-only, 184 of
those re-selections, spread evenly over papers (Gini 0.29) and positions. So the 8.7 percent yield
gap has no kind to it and no instruction remedy is indicated: R-31 closes there. What it opened is
larger. Counts agree while a quarter of claim identities do not, across arms. Whether that is the
arm or the extractor's own run-to-run variation is unmeasured, and the A/A pair that answers it
already exists on five papers. Zero model calls: match claims between the two replicates by segment
and span overlap, report the share of claims with a counterpart, per paper and pooled, with the
same matcher H-006 Part D used so the numbers are comparable.

Prior art: test-retest reliability (the term and the design are a century old in measurement);
span-matched agreement as in MUC and CoNLL evaluation, exact and partial; Krippendorff's alpha for
unitized data where the units themselves vary between coders (Krippendorff 2013, ch. 12), which is
this case exactly. The consequence, if the replicate share is near the cross-arm share: a claims
graph is one draw from a distribution, S-013's contradiction candidates inherit that, and the
remedy space (k-run intersection, self-consistency voting as in Wang et al. 2022) is a design
session and not a patch.

## R-35 The ceiling comment is corrected by record

control.yaml says 102,109,313 is "under the declared 100,000,000". It is over it. The operator's
40M authorization is the authority and nothing was exceeded; the declared ceiling IS now
102,109,313 and the file should say that.

## R-43 Claim quality is entailment, coverage and decontextualization, measured before any protocol is called best

The instrument is ai-readiness-kg's probe protocol, ported not rebuilt, extended by Claimify's two
other dimensions with its published judging prompts as the starting point. Raters are not the
extractor. It is positive-controlled before any verdict is read (methodology 7.6): planted
non-entailed claims, planted claims with unresolved referents, and a planted pack with its
verifiable sentences withheld must each be caught at or above 0.9.

## R-44 One bake-off, three arms, quality as the constraint and cost as the objective

Same 15 already-extracted documents, stratified by size, seeded draw, none touched by any earlier
arm:
- **A, per-segment (current).** Existing records; zero extraction cost.
- **B, packs with anchors** (DN-009 R-41): 1,500-token paragraph-integral packs, breadcrumb,
  harness-located anchors.
- **C, B plus the Claimify contract in one call:** the instruction asks for verifiable assertions
  only (selection), each rewritten to stand alone using the breadcrumb and the pack, added context
  in square brackets as Claimify marks it, one assertion per claim; anchor unchanged.

Pre-registered rule. FLOORS, per arm, on a seeded sample of 150 claims and 100 source sentences:
entailment by ai-readiness-kg's thresholds (F_upper < 0.10, item-faithful at or above 0.70);
anchor grounding at or above 0.98; schema validity at or above 0.98. Among arms clearing the
floors, rank by USABLE CLAIMS PER MILLION TOKENS, a usable claim being entailed AND decontextualized
AND grounded, and require sentence-level coverage at or above 0.90 of the best arm's so a sparse
cheap arm cannot win on price. Every arm's full row is reported so the operator can overrule the
ranking with the numbers in front of him. No fourth arm and no re-registration without him
(anti-spiral clause).

## R-45 What follows from the verdict is decided now, not after

If B or C wins: it becomes the protocol for the 320 remaining documents, records carry `unit` and
`emission`, and the report prices re-extracting the 530 already done at the winning arm's cost
against A's measured decontextualization rate, so the operator sees one number for a homogeneous
graph. If A wins: resume as it was, and the week's cost work stands as the answer. The cascade
(DN-008) is fitted afterwards at the winning unit; H-008 and its addendum are superseded by H-009,
which keeps their zero-call measurements. A gleaning pass is tested only if the winner's coverage
is under 0.85, because in this client it doubles the cost.

## R-46 One call runner; everything that calls a model or the network goes through it

`squiddy` gets a single runner for repeated external calls. It owns: the unit key (hash of arm or
stage, item id, rater or role, prompt hash, model, transport); the append-only fsynced JSONL
checkpoint; resume by skip; progress every 60 seconds or N units to stdout and a log; the pilot
(default 20 units or 1 percent) that prints projected tokens and wall clock and records them
before continuing; token and wall-clock ceilings from config that stop new calls, let in-flight
ones land, and exit non-zero; failures as rows under a bounded retry; aggregation over whatever
the checkpoint holds, stating n. The daemon's extraction loop, the quality instrument's raters and
scorer, corpus fetches and every future harness use it. The meter and the token bucket sit inside
it, so a call cannot be unmetered either.

## R-47 The stage fails code that goes around the runner

A static check over the package and `scripts/`: any invocation of the model client, `subprocess`
to the CLI, or an HTTP library outside the runner module fails the build, with a planted
violation as its positive control (DN-003 T-2). One kill test per consumer of the runner: SIGKILL
mid-loop, restart, final output equals an uninterrupted run's, no completed key called twice.
Tests use a stub client; they cost nothing.

## R-48 The documents say so, and task files carry the plan

This repo's CLAUDE.md gets a short section pointing at section 15 of the constitution and at the
runner, stating that a loop of external calls outside it is a defect. `docs/EXTRACTION_DESIGN_SPEC.md`
gains EX-REQ-15 (all repeated external calls go through the checkpointing runner; verified by the

other tools cite. Every Desktop task file that orders such a loop carries a checkpoint plan: unit
and key, checkpoint path, resume command, progress interval, pilot size, ceilings, what a partial
result reports. Desktop reads `~/GitHub/CLAUDE.md` at session start; not having done so is recorded
here as the defect it was.

## R-40 The methodology is a governing document of this repo, and the internal search is a gate

`kg_construction_methodology.md` is copied into `docs/` here with its source commit recorded, and
CLAUDE.md lists it among the governing documents. Every design note carries a `Prior art` section
with two parts: external literature, and the internal-precedent search (sibling repos'
`docs/research` and `docs/design`, Seldon decision logs, the project's conversation history), each
naming what was searched and what was found. Enforcement belongs in Seldon, not in each repo: an
Issue is filed there for `cc register` to refuse a task whose cited DN lacks that section. A rule
held in one repo's prose is the failure this note records.

## R-41 Packs with harness-located anchors are tested now, because that is where the money is

A squiddy call is about 1,000 fixed tokens carrying about 200 tokens of segment: over 80 percent
overhead. The cascade of DN-008 can remove at most the share of calls that find nothing. Packing
removes the overhead itself: at 1,500 tokens of text per call the fixed part falls to about 40
percent, roughly 3x on every remaining document, and it composes with the cascade.

H-002 tried 1,000-token batches, measured a 6.7x saving, and refused them on grounding (0.866 and
0.889 against 0.95). ai-readiness-kg's chunked arm PASSED its faithfulness gate at the same unit
size (F_upper 0.0458, item-faithful 1.000). The visible difference is 6.5's anchor contract:
there the harness locates a short unique anchor; here the model types the span and the harness
checks it, and typed spans drift as inputs lengthen. Hypothesis, not mechanism: H-002's grounding
loss was the emission contract, not the unit. One arm tests it: section-bounded paragraph packs,
cap 1,500 real tokens, breadcrumb, anchors located by the harness, against DN-005 R-24's frame
(pooled grounding and schema validity at or above 0.98, grounded claims at or above 0.85 of the
per-segment protocol's, on documents no arm has seen), with H-007's test-retest share beside it.
Overlap is omitted on purpose: packs are paragraph-integral, claims here are sentence-local, and
overlap would double-extract; if boundary loss shows in the claims ratio, that is the finding.

## R-42 What does not transfer is said, so the next reader does not re-import it blind

6.5's 33-46K-token outputs are not this pipeline's problem: output here is about 6 percent of a
call. 6.2 concerns typed relations; squiddy extracts claims, not relation triples, so its gate
evidence stands as measured here. Prior art sets the first hypothesis. It does not replace the
pilot.

## R-36 The oracle labels already exist, so the cascade is calibrated at zero model calls

BARGAIN calibrates on a few hundred oracle labels. This run holds one per segment for 520
documents: every call's status says whether the extractor found a grounded claim there. That is
tens of thousands of labels, free. The proxy is trained and its threshold calibrated on them,
split BY DOCUMENT (a segment-level split leaks a document's vocabulary across the line).

## R-37 The proxy is local. A cheap model tier is not cheap in this client

The literature's second tier is a small LLM. Here a call costs about 1,000 tokens before the
segment is read (H-004, H-005), so a Haiku pre-check would cost what it saves. Tiers: (0)
deterministic code, for segments that are structurally not prose: reference lists, tables of
contents, indexes, acknowledgments, numeric tables, fragments under a length floor; (1) a linear
classifier on lexical features, trained on R-36's labels, run locally. Anything heavier is
justified by measurement against tier 1 or not added.

## R-38 Quality is the constraint and cost is the objective

Pre-registered before any fit: minimize calls subject to retaining at or above 0.98 of GROUNDED
CLAIMS (claim-weighted, not segment-weighted: a skipped segment holding four claims costs four) on
held-out documents, with failure probability 0.05 by BARGAIN's recall-target procedure. Checked
separately within each document-size quartile and within the documents over 500,000 characters
already extracted, because a threshold that holds on papers and fails on books is the failure the
operator's hypothesis predicts. If no threshold saves at or above 20 percent of calls at that
recall, adopt nothing and say so.

Two things bound the claim. The labels are one draw from an extractor whose test-retest agreement
H-007 Part C is measuring; recall against a noisy oracle is recall against that draw, and the
report says so with H-007's number beside it. And a skip is recorded, never silent (R-23): the
record carries the tier, the score, the threshold and the classifier's hash, so every skipped
segment is recoverable by a later run and nothing about adoption is irreversible.

## R-39 The operator's hypothesis is measured, and the science joins the corpus

Grounded claims per 1,000 characters against document length and document kind, over the 520
extracted: zero model calls, reported whatever it shows. The works above are admitted through the
corpus's own admission path, the same one every other work came through; if that path takes only
thread citations, this note and this conversation are the citation.

## R-50 The quantity is Choi's definition, read through Newman's questions, bounded by minimality

The judge keeps Claimify's step 2, which already asks what a reader would ask and whether the
context answers it. What changes is the pass rule. A claim FAILS when the judge raises a question
of Newman's coreference or definition type that the supplied context answers and the claim does
not. Questions of the third type (more context) and questions the context cannot answer do not
fail a claim; that is Claimify's own condition and Molecular Facts' minimality. The reader model
is Newman 2.3: the reader holds the Work's title and authors and nothing else, so first-person
and "this work" references resolve. `C_max` is still emitted for audit and is no longer the test.

or what the snippet already answers).

and the report says which. Positive control: H-009's 30 plants, unchanged. 7.9 applies: a stub

and the strict both-raters share printed beside it.

One JSONL row per item per rater, written as it lands, carrying `c_max`, questions with their
type and answerability, reason, prompt sha256 and model. DN-011's runner is not built; H-011
writes its own per-unit checkpoint with resume by skip and names itself a consumer to be moved

Methodology rule 6. What the literature points at, for a later measured arm: Newman finds

## R-56 Validation against the human reference replaces the two-LLM agreement requirement on this dimension

The methodology's two-rater rule was written for entailment, where no human reference exists. Where a published human label exists, two LLMs agreeing is not validity. Plants 30 (floor 0.90, unchanged). Newman originals 40, same draw, scored against the paragraph-scope human label computed in 18.1 from the evidence field before any call. The runner checks the metered cumulative against the ceiling after every landed unit and exits non-zero at the ceiling; the pilot projection is per item kind (plant, original, arm claim) and the projection uses the longest kind. Recorded as the second instance of the DN-011 defect.

The instrument's record is: positive control passes at 0.93 to 0.97 across three runs; a two-rater design is dead because the secondary failed its plants; agreement with a published human label is 0.60 to 0.65 at n = 40 with an interval that spans the human-human figure; the label and the reader model disagree by construction on 12 of 40 items. When a task first needs the number, its first step is two further passes of 2.1.0 over the same 40 originals (about 80 calls, 0.26M at the measured rate), reporting self-agreement as positive agreement, negative agreement and AC1, and majority-of-three as the verdict if self-agreement is under 0.90. ## R-62 Downstream questions before any further extraction-quality work

The graph's competency questions (what a consumer asks the claims graph, EX-REQ-14) are written as the next design work, at zero model calls, before H-010 and before any arm is touched. Decontextualization is measured again only if a written question needs a claim to stand alone.

## R-63 A control's power is stated before its bar

Every future pre-registered bar on a proportion states n, the Wilson half-width at that n, and whether the bar is distinguishable from the null at that width. A bar that is not is written as a report line, not a gate. Sections 17 and 18 are the two instances.

## R-69 R-67 does not cover emitter, verb, ledger-ingest or release work

R-67 holds extraction, arms, protocols, judges and the daemon. The four findings are emitter, serve and ingest defects and are repaired now, at zero model calls. A repair that touches a prompt, a model client or the extraction unit is out of scope and is refused by the task.

The harvest lesson carries every (conversation_id, first_mention_date, mention_count) triple for its work; the `CitedIn` emit block iterates them. Every Conversation the export names that cited at least one admitted entry becomes a node. Gates: Person count unchanged (DI-064); every pre-existing CitedIn edge still present with its properties; new edge count equals the distinct (work, conversation) pairs in `citations.tsv` for admitted works, computed before the emit and compared after; S-009's parity legs green on the new release.

`squiddy extract ingest` over every record on disk not yet in the ledger, zero model calls; the span re-read and hash gate on every claim; the count of ingested, refused and already-present recorded; a release cut after. `Q001_claim_reachable_text_share` is re-measured from 0.0024.

All 17 requirement questions, three arms, k = 10, receipts captured, 19.4's five preconditions measured and written first, 19.5's mechanical score per arm per question, per-archetype tables with Wilson intervals, and the retrieved-set overlap per question. The result ranks nothing (R-63; n under 20 everywhere) and is the first measurement of arm A on this graph and the first end-to-end run of the instrument. A precondition that fails stops the run.

The judge harness: prompt frozen to a file, pointwise and pairwise calls, both presentation orders, sealed mapping written before the first judgment and its sha256 recorded before it is read, the two calibration probes (a seeded irrelevant set must score 0; a seeded dominant pair must win in both orders). All of it tested against a stub judge. At run time the harness checks `docs/q001/gemini_questions_raw.md` and the key through the accessor; either missing is an availability state written to the report, and the demand half does not run.

## R-78 Two remainders from Q-002 are closed on the way

An enumeration verb `list_entries(class, where)` over the served release (CQ-004, CQ-005), added to `ARM_T_MECHANISM.md` before the first query. And the write-path defect Q-002 found (a re-asserted edge with changed properties is dropped instead of updated, 138 stale `mentions`): `squiddy.write` compares properties on a keyed re-assertion and emits an update event; positive control T-2 with one planted property change; the parity legs green after.

## R-64 Two question classes, both registered and typed by archetype: requirement questions from scenarios on record, and demand questions the operator supplies

`docs/COMPETENCY_QUESTIONS.md` holds the set. Each question carries: the scenario it comes from, with the document that records the scenario (FIRST_CONSUMER.md, a DN, a DI row, an HV or H task's stated purpose, or a served verb's docstring); its archetype from a fixed list of five, taken from Han et al. and Wiśniewski et al. (single-hop lookup; multi-hop traversal; comparison across works; temporal or supersession; aggregation over a set); the answer's form (a set of node keys, a number, a span); and the ground-truth source, which is never the graph itself. Questions the graph answers by construction (a citation event's conversation is an edge the emitter wrote) are lookups and are marked so; they measure integrity, not usefulness. The library graph is the subject; biblio's verbs are its precedent. These are the REQUIREMENT class (Grüninger-Fox): known answers, mechanical ground truth, written by the task from the record. The DEMAND class is G4's in regime and not in authorship (operator amendment 2026-09-23: "this is building the builder for KG", the questions are not his to write). They are authored by an independent model, Gemini, blind to the graph, prompted from the consumer's stated purpose and the corpus inventory (`docs/q001/GEMINI_PROMPT_demand_questions.md`, `docs/q001/corpus_inventory_for_question_authoring.md`, 933 titled works, 301 repositories, 218 thread names, zero model calls to build), 24 questions at fixed counts per archetype with the four lookups as the search-should-win control. The reply is saved verbatim as `docs/q001/gemini_questions_raw.md`, frozen with a shuffle seed, typed as Gemini typed them unless a type is plainly wrong (recorded), never edited. The same model later judges the arms' blinded answers (R-66), which keeps the judge independent of the extractor (sonnet) and the quality rater (opus). Caveat on the record: G4's doctrine line says synthetic questions test the instrument and operator questions test the value; a domain-aware author who never sees the system is the Cranfield posture and sits between the two, and the corpus-gap rule catches questions the corpus cannot hold.

## R-65 Ground truth comes from outside the graph, and completeness is measured before retrieval

For every REQUIREMENT question the ground truth is one of: an external authority record (OpenAlex, Crossref, DataCite, already cached under `evidence/20260915_hv003/openalex_records/`); a span located exactly once in an acquired text by the same locator the extractor uses; or an operator-independent derivation from the source documents recorded as code. No requirement question is admitted whose ground truth would have to be judged by a model or labelled by the operator; demand questions have no ground truth by design and are scored by R-66. Before any retrieval is compared, the share of ground-truth entities present in the served graph is measured and reported per archetype (Han's 65.5 percent is the reference); a graph missing the answer cannot be blamed on its retriever.

## R-66 The downstream test is G4's instrument, pre-registered per archetype, with the published direction as the null

When the test runs (not in this task), it is G4's design re-instantiated: arm T the served graph's verbs, arm A FTS plus S-013's pinned local encoder with frozen fusion, arm L lexical-only as diagnostic, one corpus allow-list bound at query time and asserted post hoc in every arm, T against A only, ties lose. Requirement questions score by exact set match or located span. Demand questions score by G4's blinded pairwise judge in both orders with the order flip a tie, pointwise 0/1/2 for the corpus-gap rule, mapping sealed until hashed, self-preference risk declared. Before any scoring, the three structural facts G4 measured are measured here: relationship types non-empty (the density gate already reports 8), reachability of the corpus by each arm, and retrieved-set overlap between arms per question; a disjoint retrieval is reported before the judge sees it. The pre-registered expectation, from Han and Xiang: the graph loses or ties on single-hop lookup and must win on multi-hop, comparison, temporal and aggregation to justify itself. A graph that wins only where embeddings already win has not passed. Rules section 19 carries the bars before the test runs; R-63 applies, so each bar states n and its half-width, and archetypes with fewer than 20 questions are report lines.

**R-79 Grounding is measured on what the protocol serves.** The 0.98 grounding floor was written for arm A, which repairs or drops nothing at birth. Arms B and C quarantine a claim whose anchor does not locate exactly once (EX-REQ-01), so every claim they SERVE is located, and the shortfall H-009 reported (0.976, 0.970) is the quarantine share. A served claim under B or C is grounded by construction and the span re-read gate (HV-008 Part D, Q-002: 26,960 of 26,960) is the check. So: grounding floor 0.98 applies to grounded over (grounded plus ungrounded, excluding quarantined); quarantine is its own line with rules 16.9's ceiling of 0.05, reported as yield loss. Nanopublication and PROV practice: an assertion without a locatable provenance is not published, and unpublished is not the same as wrong.

Under R-79 both B and C clear the floors. Coverage: C 0.750, B 0.327, A 0.154; the 0.90-of-best condition leaves C. `F_upper`: all under 0.10. ## R-81 A cascade with pre-registered gates, not a bet

The daemon runs arm C as its protocol.
