- **R-103 (statistical quality control on every unit operation).** Every unit operation carries
  pre-registered gates, planted controls that prove each gate fires (X-001), metered spend, and a
  kill rule whose firing stops the line and opens an assignable-cause investigation before anything
  restarts. Q-004 is the template for that investigation. Floors are set before data and moved only
  by a logged correction to a pre-registered rule (DN-021), never after the fact.

- **R-104 (products differ; fundamentals do not).** The invariant core every graph gets from the
  kit: the identity spine, the event-sourced ledger with the store as a rebuildable projection,
  grounding spans located at birth, the administrative layer (OpenAlex or the domain's authority),
  entity resolution with recoverable merges, drift and parity gates, conformance gates with
  controls, versioned releases, and one MCP surface generated from the graph's schema. The product
  type (policy graph, evidence graph, readiness graph, exercise-science graph) is a schema, a
  recipe and a gate configuration, never new machinery. Whether the surfaces should converge on a
  universal connector contract is tabled at the operator's word.

- **R-105 (continuous maintenance is a product function).** Scheduled unit operations, never
  unbounded agents: admission of a new document (one file, one command, minutes, extraction shown
  before commit); supersession and retirement by logged events (built); currency sweeps;
  measure-before-commit re-extraction when a better model appears (DI-026); and refutation, which
  is new: when later evidence contradicts a recorded claim, the contradiction is a logged
  adjudication attached to both claims, never a deletion (DI-044). Refutation is a research problem
  with prior art (SciFact and its successors) and gets its own pre-registered design before it is
  built.

- **R-106 (the served surface is decided by evidence per graph).** What a product serves is the
  outcome of that graph's own downstream test, run as a unit operation with a valve, before bulk
  spend (X-001 item 18). A claims layer is served where it beats the baseline on the graph's own
  questions; where it does not, metadata plus full text plus concepts is the product and claims
  are an overlay the surface may cite. The factory therefore builds the cheap layers first and
  earns the expensive ones.

- **R-110 (the primary verb is hybrid retrieval with receipts).** `search(question, k)` over
  paragraph units and metadata documents: FTS5 plus the pinned dense index, fused by RRF exactly
  as arm A ran (its parameters frozen and cited to Q-003 Part 0 and S-008 19.2). Every hit carries
  a located receipt: Expression key, page, character offsets, or `record` for a metadata document.
  Arm A's code is promoted from `squiddy/arms.py` into the kit as the `index` unit operation, built
  at release time for every graph, with an index-parity gate (index rows equal the release's units
  and metadata documents, by count and hash).

- **R-111 (the bibliographic structure is navigation, served as verbs).** `work`, `expressions`,
  `cites` and `cited_by` (where a Cites layer exists; on this graph the citation events and threads),
  `threads`, `topics_of`, `works_on_topic`, `concepts_of`, `mentions`. These are authority data and
  were never on trial. `discover` stays, repaired, reported for what it reaches.

- **R-112 (claims are an overlay, never a retrieval index).** `claims_in(receipt)` returns the
  grounded claims located within a hit's span, with their spans and provenance. Claims are not
  searched, ranked or hopped to; they annotate text the primary verb found. No claim is deleted or
  retired; the ledger keeps every event. Whether the overlay adds value over bare text is untested
  and is not claimed; it costs nothing to serve. The extraction valve for future graphs is closed
  by default (R-106, X-001 item 18) and opens only when that graph's own downstream test earns it.

- **R-113 (Arnold's recipe).** The second consumer is built from the cheap layers only: catalog,
  acquisition, administrative layer, structure-aware units, index, concept mentions by scanning,
  citation and metadata structure, release, MCP surface. Its competency questions are generated by
  the machine from its purpose statement (R-102), and its downstream test runs on that surface
  first. S-010's recipe is this ruling; the precedes hold from DN-022 R-97 is released by it.

- **R-114 (one MCP contract per graph, generated from the schema).** The served verbs above are
  the contract, rendered from `graph.yaml` and the index manifest; a graph without a claims layer
  serves the same contract with `claims_in` returning empty. The universal-connector question
  beyond the kit's own graphs stays tabled at the operator's word.

- **R-133 (library is the proving ground; Arnold waits).** The first real run of `squiddy build`
  is on library, not Arnold: a full build from library's intake on a fresh copy (the K-002 shape,
  with the index), then the maintenance loop on the served library graph. S-010 waits on both.

- **R-134 (incremental dense keying before any maintenance run).** The index unit keys per
  document: each admitted entry's chunks are cut and encoded as one resumable unit with a fixed
  padding width, so admitting or superseding one document re-keys that document only. The
  comparison is pre-registered against A-equivalence on the 24 demand questions at k = 10
  (S-016 A.4's leg, 21 of 24 byte-identical is the floor; a tie decided by row id is not a
  difference) and against wall clock: admit-one must re-key in under five minutes on library.

- **R-135 (the maintenance loop is demonstrated as one run, with every event of record).** On the
  served library graph, through the factory's maintenance entries, in this order: admit one new
  document the operator did not choose (the machine picks a work cited by the corpus and not held,
  from the administrative layer); supersede one held preprint by its published expression (an
  HV-004 pair); run the currency sweep; cut the release; run the anchors and index-parity gates;
  serve; touch STOP mid-run once and resume. Every step is a ledger event; the status view is
  captured at each step; the served surface answers a query on the new document afterwards. The
  demand test is not re-run (it is bound to its release and costs about 464k tokens; R-126's dated
  re-test line is the operator's if he wants it).

- **R-136 (what "ready for Arnold" means, so it can be checked and not felt).** R-134's floor and
  bound met; R-135 run green with its evidence; the full-build run green; `init --check` clean on
  library or every drift named; the touchpoint count on both runs exactly the pauses R-121 lists
  and no other. Then S-010's first action is `squiddy init` in the Arnold repo with `scope.topic`
  in the operator's words.

- **R-137 (decisions and acquisition answers are inputs of a build).** The input wall carries
  three things, not one: the intake, the graph's decision record (the manifest's decided entries
  with their reasons and provenance) and the acquisition record (K-002's records log, imported
  once as keyed records of the factory's acquire node). A build that receives a decision record
  applies it before the graph's criterion: a decided entry is not undecided, and only entries the
  record does not cover reach R-127's pause. So a rebuild of a served graph pauses at nothing
  (M-001 A.2 holds for rebuilds) and a first build of a new graph pauses once, by design, with
  the plan report (R-127 holds for first builds). Resolver answers are read from the acquisition
  record by unit key; a request leaves the machine only for an entry the record does not hold.

- **R-138 (every served layer is produced by a node; the census is the coverage gate).** Each
  class in a served graph's census names the factory node that produces it, in the graph's emit
  spec. A class with no producing node fails a conformance gate (no orphan layer), with a planted
  orphan as the control. Under this rule library's DAG gains: `resolve` (HV-003/HV-004 identity
  merges, before write); text attachment inside `acquire` (HV-005, which today runs as
  `tools/attach_texts.py`); `admin` as both a build node and a maintenance unit M-06 for Works in
  the pending slice; `concepts` (HV-006's scan) under a valve of its own, zero model calls; a
  second intake source for standards, since `catalog` takes N sources. Claim stays the extract
  valve's.

- **R-139 (identifier lookups bind to the registration agency).** When an entry is cataloged from
  an identifier, the title, authors and container of record are the registration agency's
  (Crossref, DataCite, arXiv for its own ids); an aggregator's `display_name` is a hint and is
  recorded beside it as `title_aggregator`. A similarity below the gate's threshold between the
  two is an `authority_conflict` event, and the entry is cataloged under the registered title.
  The M-001 pick is corrected by this rule as a maintenance event, not re-admitted.

- **R-140 (currency findings feed a repair unit, M-07).** For each id the sweep reports not
  current: a DOI that fails ISO 26324 syntax is stripped, and the expression is re-resolved by
  title and authors through the registration agencies; a syntactically valid DOI answering 404 is
  re-queried once at the agency and once at OpenAlex, then recorded `unresolved` with the date; an
  OpenAlex work id that no longer resolves is re-resolved by DOI. Every outcome is a ledger event
  on the expression; an expression that ends with no valid identifier keeps its text and its
  citation string and loses only the key. X-001 item 16's key gate extends to Expression DOIs.

- **R-141 (readiness after this note).** R-136's failing row is re-run as M-002: the full build
  on a fresh copy with the decision and acquisition records carried, every layer produced by a
  node, and the census matching the served census class for class. S-010 waits on M-002.

- **R-129 (the input is a scope statement in the operator's words).** The block is renamed
  `scope:`. Required: `topic`, a paragraph in the operator's words naming the collection he wants
  (exercise science and martial arts; federal AI readiness; the KG-construction literature).
  Optional: `anchors`, sources, ideas or phrases he already knows the graph must cover;
  `exclusions`, what it must not become (the AI-washing case). No field asks for questions, a
  class of questions, or intended uses. `init` requires only `topic`. R-102's "what it exists to
  answer, as a class" and R-121 item 3's wording are amended to this; touchpoint 3 is the scope
  statement and anything the operator later adds to it.

- **R-130 (competency questions are the machine's instrument).** The `questions` node generates
  them from the corpus plus the scope statement (the Rebboud/Alharbi line, as Q-001 ADDENDUM 02
  already ran); they test the build against the pre-registered bar and never specify it. The
  operator may add questions and never gates on a verdict (R-102, unchanged). `anchors` become a
  coverage gate at release, not questions: every anchor resolves to at least one located receipt
  through the served verbs, with a planted missing anchor as the positive control.

- **R-131 (the question set grows with use).** The served surface logs every query it answers
  (verb, arguments, receipts returned, timestamp) to `<graph>/factory/queries.jsonl`, local to the
  graph, never shipped, controlled by `serve.log_queries` in the control file (required key,
  default in the template `true`). The maintenance-time demand test draws its questions from that
  log plus a fresh generated set, so utility is measured on what was actually asked and the
  instrument follows the exploration (Bates 1989). A query is data, never an instruction to the
  factory.

- **R-132 ("throw a video against the literature" is a verb).** `check(text or transcript)`:
  segment the input, `search` each segment, return the located receipts that support or
  contradict it, with `claims_in` as the overlay where a claims layer exists. It is the front door
  of the refutation unit (R-105) and is recorded here as a product verb candidate for Arnold,
  built after refutation's own design note; the intake side is the existing `ingest-youtube`
  skill. Not part of F-001.

- **R-147. Text availability is a catalog attribute.** For every candidate, the plan report shows its text
  route, its license and the host that route needs, before the admit decision. Routes: local, PMC (Cloud Service,
  E-utilities or BioC), Europe PMC REST, Unpaywall best OA location, none. An admit decision records whether
  text is expected. "Metadata only, knowingly" is a valid admit.

- **R-148. Acquire takes the routes built for automated access, in that order, never a website scrape.** Each
  route is a declared bucket. A host that a route returns and that is not declared is a plan-report line, not a
  silent refusal at the forwarder. PMID and PMCID citations resolve through the ID Converter.

- **R-149. Release gate `text_held`.** Every admitted entry is either text-held or carries a no-text reason from
  a closed list: `admitted_metadata_only`, `not_oa`, `route_refused:<host>`, `license`, `no_identifier`. An
  entry admitted with text expected that arrives without text fails the release, with a planted control. No
  numeric floor: the gate catches the surprise, and an entry admitted knowingly without text passes.

- **R-150. A test verdict records the text coverage of the release it ran on.** A verdict computed on a release
  that failed or skipped `text_held` registers as not interpretable, and kills nothing.

- **R-151. A delivery report leads with any admitted-versus-held gap.** It is the first table, before the
  registered results.

- **R-152. Seeds come from the scope, mapped onto MeSH.** The seed terms are the scope topic's listed subjects, in
  the operator's words. Each is sent to the MeSH lookup service; the candidates it returns are the only vocabulary.
  A model call may choose among the returned descriptors for a seed, with a one-line rationale per choice recorded.
  A seed with no fitting descriptor is reported as such, with no substitute invented.

- **R-153. Queries are built from descriptors by rule, not by model.** Per descriptor: `[MeSH Major Topic]`,
  restricted to the declared publication types, on E-utilities, through the forwarder. A per-descriptor cap `k`
  is declared in the spec (default 5, PubMed's relevance order). Results are deduplicated across descriptors and
  against the manifest.

- **R-154. Candidates enter the catalog with their DN-032 route.** The plan report shows, per candidate: the seed
  and descriptor that found it, the publication type, the text route and host. Admission stays the operator's
  touchpoint 3.

- **R-155. Anchors are marked from the descriptor list.** The plan report lists the chosen descriptors; the
  operator may mark any of them as anchors at the same touchpoint. Anchors stay the operator's prior knowledge,
  expressed in the field's vocabulary.

- **R-156. The seeded search is a kit intake source, inside the DAG.** It replaces nothing: the shelf sources stay.
  `squiddy catalog --from` runs through the forwarder (ACQ-001 closed finding 14); this source does too.

- **R-157. Every held text records its licence, on every graph.** Values: the SPDX-style identifier the source
  states, or `unstated` for a local file that states none. Recording never refuses anything.

- **R-158. One spec key, `visibility: public | private`, default `public`.** No other switch is added.
  - `public` (the default; library and every graph without the key): unchanged from today. The licence allowlist
    binds text attachment, and `publish` refuses any release holding a text whose licence is not on the allowlist.
  - `private`: the allowlist binds nothing a local file the operator admits; the `publish` valve cannot be opened
    (a FATAL at config load if it is set open), so private content has no path out through the kit.

- **R-159. Changing `private` to `public` is a release-level check, not a migration.** The next release runs the
  allowlist over every held text and refuses until each is allowlisted or removed. Nothing is re-ingested.

- **R-142 (network policy is per process and deny-by-default).** Every process the factory
  starts, and `squiddy serve`, runs under a declared network policy: `none` or a list of HTTP
  buckets. `none` is enforced two ways at once: `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` set to a
  closed local port with `NO_PROXY` empty, and on macOS a `sandbox-exec` profile denying network,
  when the kit can apply it. A node with buckets gets the real network for those hosts only
  (the proxy is the call layer's own allowlisting forwarder). `serve` is `none` always.

- **R-143 (offline is set at kit import, not at use).** `squiddy/__init__.py` sets
  `HF_HUB_OFFLINE`, `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE` and `HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY` before any import of
  the ML stack, and every entry point (`serve`, `index`, `arms`, `concepts`, tools) imports the
  kit first. A module that imports `transformers`, `sentence_transformers` or `huggingface_hub`
  before the kit fails a test.

- **R-144 (the egress check is dynamic; the static check is kept, not trusted alone).** The suite
  gains an egress tier: every entry point and every node whose policy is `none` is started under
  R-142's closed network on the fixture graph and must succeed; a planted library-level call (a
  stub module that opens a socket at import) must fail it. The static check stays for kit source.
  No "offline" or "no network" claim appears in a docstring, spec or report without naming the
  egress test that proves it.

- **R-145 (incident handling, this incident).** X-002 captures the exact request with a logging
  proxy on a copy with the fix disabled; checks for a token and, if one exists, the operator
  revokes it (touchpoint: a credential only he holds); restarts the Claude Desktop server under
  the fix; audits every encoder load site in this repo, Wintermute and Arnold for the same
  defect; records the incident in `factory/incidents/` and in Seldon; and the delivery report of
  every task since S-016 that declared "no network" gains an erratum line naming this incident.

- **R-146 (the lesson, codified).** A third-party library is an external caller. The kit's
  boundary is the process, not the source tree. Lesson file for the conformance set; EX-REQ-15 is
  restated: every external call is declared, metered, and PROVEN absent where undeclared by a
  closed-network run.

- **R-160 (revises R-152). The model may propose lookup labels; it still chooses only returned descriptors.** Per
  seed, at most 5 proposed labels (for example "range of motion" for "mobility"), each sent to the lookup. The guard
  is unchanged: a descriptor the service did not return cannot be chosen.

- **R-161 (revises R-153). Every descriptor query carries the scope's context block.** The spec declares context
  descriptors, resolved through the same lookup; for Arnold that is exercise, sports and physical fitness. A topic
  descriptor outside the context's MeSH tree is ANDed with the context block. One inside it runs alone. The plan
  report shows hits with and without the block.

- **R-162 (replaces ADDENDUM 01 Part C's screen). The shelf is screened by a model on the title and first page,
  sensitivity first.** Verdicts are include, exclude or unsure, and unsure goes to the plan report. The recall
  control is the operator's nine named fitness texts: all nine must pass, or the screen is not used and the run
  stops. The precision measure is the pass count and the SEED-001 false positives it drops, reported, not gated.

- **R-163. Disk preflight and bounded scratch.** Before its first item, every factory run checks free space on the
  data volume and the temp directory against a spec floor (default 25 GB), and stops with a recorded reason below it.
  The check repeats every progress interval. A run's scratch lives under the graph directory, never an unbounded
  temp tree.

- **R-164 (revises R-162's gate). A control file passes when the model judged it and did not exclude it.** `include`
  or `unsure`, with a model call made, passes. An `exclude` is a miss and fails the gate. A verdict reached with no
  call fails the gate as a reader failure, reported apart from misses. Every control file must be reached and judged
  before the gate is read.

- **R-165. The reader gives the model something to judge.**
  - Page one with no text: the file name, with extension and shadow-library suffixes stripped, is sent as the
    title, with a model call.
  - Page one under 400 characters of text: the excerpt extends through page 3, or until 2,000 characters.
  - EPUB: the package title and the first chapter's first 2,000 characters.
  - OCR is not added now. It is the next step if R-164 still finds reader failures.

- **R-166. A verdict is keyed on the exact excerpt sent.** The unit key is the sha256 of the template, the scope and
  the excerpt text, not the excerpt-length setting. A file whose excerpt R-165 does not change keeps its recorded
  verdict and costs no call.

- **R-167. The positive control runs in a segment built for it.** A synthetic paragraph containing the control
  sentence and no other claim is passed to the extract prompt as its own segment, attached to the first worklist
  paper's provenance. The expected output is the control sentence. A pass or failure measures the instrument only.
  Library's earlier passes stand; its next pilot uses R-167 too.

- **R-168. An expression key reads a PMID.** The order is DOI, then arXiv id, then PMID (`pmid:<n>`) resolved to a
  Work through OpenAlex, then the entry's own identifier as `work_key` (KG-001's graph-level correction, now in the
  kit). Conformance item 19 must pass on a fixture graph with PMID-only and book entries and no graph-level correction.

- **R-169. Reserve before dispatch.** A paper is dispatched only if, with `B` the largest projected or measured paper
  cost on this graph so far, spent plus `B` for each paper in flight plus `B` for the new paper is no more than the
  ceiling. The projection is corrected with the measured cost as papers finish. STOP is checked between segments as
  well as between papers, and a paper stopped mid-way resumes at its next segment.

- **R-170. The stable prompt comes first.**
  - The extract call puts the template, schema and instructions (everything constant across calls) ahead of the
    segment text, in the position the transport caches.
  - A self-test of three consecutive calls on one template must show cache reads on calls 2 and 3, or the run stops.
  - The meter reports the cache read share for each run.

- **R-171. Ungrounded rows are audited before the gate is read.**
  - Each ungrounded row is classed with its evidence: verifier false negative (the claim text is in the source after
    whitespace, hyphenation or ligature normalization), or real (the wording is not in the source).
  - A false negative is fixed in the verifier, with a test from that row, and every record is re-verified at zero
    model cost.
  - The gate threshold does not change.

- **R-172. On Arnold the extraction valve stays closed.**
  - SQ-004 and KG-006 are superseded.
  - DN-039's two kit defects are recorded as an Issue for any graph that opens extraction later. They are real: the
    ceiling bounds dispatch rather than spend, and the prefix is uncacheable. They are not built now.
  - DN-038 R-167 and R-168 stand. They are merged, and R-168 (the PMID expression key) serves every graph.

- **R-173. Arnold's concept layer is MeSH, held, from two sources.**
  1. The NLM annual descriptor file, held as the graph's vocabulary: descriptors, entry terms, tree numbers. It is
     scanned over every held text by the kit's existing mention scanner.
  2. Each PubMed-indexed Work's NLM-assigned MeSH headings, attached as authority-tagged concepts. These come from the
     PubMed records the routes already fetch, or one E-utilities fetch per PMID.

  Done means `mentions` and `discover` answer from text on KG-004's smoke questions, and conformance item 19 reports
  `MentionsConcept` built. No model calls.

- **R-174. A decision-record field is never overwritten by a derived value.**
  - A field set by the operator's decision record outranks the same field derived by any node. Today that means
    `text_expected` and `no_text_reason`; R-147 already names them, and other fields are listed as found.
  - This holds both in what a node writes and in what its `completed()` compares, so such an entry is never re-pended.
  - The kit provides one function, used by every node that writes manifest fields, and a test runs each such node
    twice over a fixture graph holding a knowing metadata-only admit.
  - Entries already damaged are restored by a kit command from the decision record, with a correction line, never by
    hand.

- **R-175. Release gates: cheap first, all reported, then the kill.**
  - Gates that read only the manifest, evidence and export run before the index stage: conformance, schema, dangling,
    `text_held`, and anchors when the anchors need no index.
  - Every stage-15 gate runs even after one fails. The release is killed once, with one incident listing every
    failing gate.
  - A failing cheap gate stops the cut before the index is built.
  - Test: a fixture with one item-5 failure and one `text_held` failure produces one incident naming both, and builds
    no index.

- **R-176. One machine-wide spend ledger, reserve then settle.** Every model call from any Squiddy process (the call
  layer, the extraction daemon, judges, screens) reserves its projected cost on one append-only ledger shared by every
  graph on the machine (`~/.squiddy/spend/ledger.jsonl`, flock-guarded, fsynced), and settles the actual from the call's
  own usage metadata. In-flight reservations count against every limit. A reservation that would cross a limit is
  refused before the call is sent. An orphan reservation is released only when its PID is dead, never by age.
  Check: concurrency test with two workers cannot exceed a limit; SIGKILL test leaves no reservation held by a dead PID
  after the next acquire.

- **R-177. Every job carries a measured estimate.** A job is a run of `squiddy build`, a maintenance lane, a task's
  model work, or any looping unit. Its estimate is the measured per-unit rate for the same model, profile and node
  (ledger history or a recorded dry run) times planned units, stored with its basis. A job with no estimate, or with an
  estimate below the measured floor, is refused. The estimator models call timing against the prompt-cache window:
  units spaced beyond the window are costed at cache-write, not cache-read. Check: refusal tests for both cases;
  estimator test on two recorded timing patterns.

- **R-178. Bands against the estimate.** Projected spend (settled plus reserved) at or under +10% over estimate: run
  and log. Crossing +10%: one `spend_warning` event. A reservation that would cross +20%: refused; the job pauses at the
  spend touchpoint and resumes only with the operator's dated approval file beside the control file
  (`spend_approval.yaml`: operator, date, job, new ceiling, words). Check: planted overrun fixture emits the warning at
  +10% and stops before the call that would pass +20%.

- **R-179. Dual caps and a storm breaker.** Each job carries a token cap and a call cap. A rolling error-rate breaker
  stops the lane (starting value 0.30 errors over the last 50 calls, from Wintermute S20, recalibrated on this kit's
  data). Daily or weekly quota errors are never retried. Check: breaker fixture; quota-error fixture makes one call.

- **R-180. Cacheable prefix.** The extraction prompt is split into a stable prefix (instructions, schema, examples)
  and a per-unit suffix, so the prefix is written once per cache window and read thereafter. Check: on a 5-call smoke
  run inside one window, calls 2 to 5 report cache-read tokens for the prefix.

- **R-181. Estimate versus actual, every job.** Each job's end writes estimate, actual, ratio and the unit count to the
  ledger; `squiddy spend report` prints per job and per lane, and the release report charts the ratio as an
  individuals chart with control limits. Token classes are recorded separately (input, output, cache write, cache
  read) with configurable weights; the default weights are the published API price ratios, recorded as an assumption
  because the Max plan's limit accounting is not published.

**Default to CLI invocation via bash for all tool use. MCP is justified only by a specific, identifiable need for structured mid-reasoning I/O.**

The burden of justification is on MCP, not CLI. When designing new tools:
1. Build the CLI first.
2. Add an MCP wrapper only when CLI-via-bash has demonstrated a concrete reasoning-loop problem that MCP solves.

When evaluating existing tools:

text:
**Wintermute's architectural center is the sleep-function layer: offline graph cognition that runs asynchronously, operates on the accumulated graph with whole-graph visibility, and improves graph fidelity over time without user intervention at ingestion time.**

Three sleep functions define this layer (full specs in CC5 deliverable):

- **A. Collapse / Dedup** — nightly. Three-layer entity resolution: deterministic SemHash pre-dedup → LLM-proposed merges (auto-accept ≥ 0.90, arbitration 0.50–0.89) → human YAML review.
- **B. Disambiguate** — weekly. Detects entities that should be split based on claim embedding bimodality, attribute contradictions, edge-type entropy. All splits go to human arbitration.
- **C. LLM-Proposed Edge Inference** — weekly, after A and B. Proposes new edges between entities with shared neighbors + embedding cosine ≥ 0.60. Same three-tier authority model as A.

**Every Wintermute engineering investment must serve these functions or the infrastructure that makes them possible.** Ingestion pipelines that generate raw entity/claim/document nodes are in-scope because sleep functions need them. Retrieval endpoints are second-class unless they serve sleep-function quality (e.g., surfacing arbitration queues).

**Commodity capture is explicitly OUT of Wintermute's core.** Per operator decision 2026-04-18, **claude-mem is adopted (Option A)** as the capture layer. Wintermute consumes claude-mem observations via bridge and owns the sleep layer above them. This is a deliberate narrowing: Wintermute does not re-solve a problem claude-mem has already solved.

**AGPL acceptance:** The claude-mem Option A commitment inherits AGPL. Acceptable for personal infrastructure (operator's context). If Seldon/Wintermute ever enters a distribution or service context where AGPL becomes restrictive, Option B (extract patterns) remains reversible at the cost of rebuilding reliability work. Flagged here so future consumers of this AD can find the assumption.

text:
Project-init bootstrap state is now data, not code. Templates are YAML files under `seldon/templates/` loaded by `seldon.templates.loader`.

Template schema (minimum required keys, extensible):

```yaml
name: <str>                # must match filename stem
description: <str>         # human-readable one-liner
bootstrap_tasks:           # list, may be empty
  - description: <str>
    name: <str>            # optional
```

Unrecognized top-level keys are preserved in the loaded dict so that future extensions (directory scaffolding, `seldon.yaml` overrides, template composition) can be added without breaking the loader contract.

`seldon init <project_name>` accepts:

- `--template <name>` (default `blank`) — selects which template to apply.
- `--list-templates` — enumerate available templates and exit.
- `--force` — proceed even if the target Neo4j database already contains artifacts.

The selected template name is recorded at `project.template` in the generated `seldon.yaml` so the init decision is auditable and reproducible.

Two templates ship:

- **`blank`** — empty. The default. Appropriate for any project where the user wants to write their own tasks.
- **`paper`** — the five `SETUP-01..05` manuscript tasks from the prior hardcoded list. Preserves onboarding for paper projects; opt-in via `--template paper`.

A secondary `init` hardening change is bundled with this AD: `init` now verifies the target Neo4j database contains no Artifact nodes before proceeding, and fails loudly if it does. `--force` overrides for explicit re-init. This closes the silent-attach gap where two directories with colliding slugs could unknowingly write to the same database.

- **AD-033-R2. One write path, control-type at the source.** Records are written only by `seldon decision`

  (forked chain; the refusal names the live head). Each file carries `prev_hash` (the previous record in that

text:
- **AD-033-R11. The log is the record of truth; Neo4j is the live working store; files are rendered views.**
  For every graph Squiddy builds, every Seldon project and this register: the authoritative record is the
  append-only, hash-chained event ledger kept with the repository. Neo4j is the live working store: every read and

  YAML and `REGISTER.md` are rendered and never hand-edited. AD-030-R5's "the manifest lives in the graph" means

  a subset of it, which is how every database including Neo4j already works (its transaction log); Kleppmann 2017
  (Designing Data-Intensive Applications, ch. 11 and 12: the log as system of record, databases as derived views);
  Kreps 2013 (The Log); 21 CFR 11.10(e) and ALCOA+ (an audit trail that never obscures what was recorded); the
  operator's own requirement that the manifest prove every past decline, which a store updated in place cannot do.

text:
**No operation reports success until it has observed its own effect.** A write that cannot demonstrate its effect via read-back is a failure, regardless of whether the underlying calls threw.

Four ratified rulings (Brock, 2026-06-10):

1. **Initial scope — five paths first, generalize later.** The invariant applies immediately to: `log_workout`, `complete_as_written`, `complete_with_deviations`, the Ultrahuman sync (`scripts/sync/ultrahuman_to_postgres.py`), and CC task closure (git↔Seldon). These paths account for the majority of class-D and class-A instances. All other write paths adopt the invariant as they are next touched.

2. **PG↔Neo4j mechanism — both in-handler verification and a reconciliation sweep.** (a) In-handler: write PG, write Neo4j, read back both, fail loudly if either is missing. (b) A scheduled reconciliation sweep diffs the two stores independently of any handler. The sweep is the standing detector for future class-A bypass paths the handlers don't own.

3. **Failure behavior — fail loudly + quarantine, not rollback fiction.** No distributed transaction exists between Postgres and Neo4j; "atomic dual-write" is unimplementable. When the second store fails: the PG row is flagged (`needs_graph_ref`), the tool response states exactly that, and the reconciliation sweep repairs the quarantine queue. Visible-but-messy beats clean-but-fictional. Silent partial success is the failure mode this ADR exists to kill.

4. **Response contract — verified counts in every success response.** Write-tool success responses include observed effect, not assertion: "wrote 9 blocks / 36 sets, read-back verified 36/36, Neo4j ref confirmed" — never bare "success." Verification is thereby visible in every transcript and log.

**Parent:** `013-canonical-training-vocabulary.md`
**Overrides:** ADR-013 "R2" wording "microcycle = ~1 wk scheduling unit", "microcycles = derived mechanically from existing `week_number`/`week_count`", and the CLAUDE.md row "~1 week | microcycle".
**Does not touch:** R1 (block = within-workout grouping), R3, the `:Cycle` base type, the `cycle_type` discriminator, or the unruled D11 concurrent-cycle question.

## What was wrong

ADR-013's structure (one `:Cycle` type, discriminator, duration) already allows variable
length. Two things baked one modality's calendar into it anyway:

1. **The prose fixed the microcycle at ~1 week** and seeded micros from `week_number`. The ADR's
   own cited source does not: Bompa gives a microcycle range of roughly 4–14 days, ~7 typical.
   The ADR kept the typical value and dropped the range.
2. **`src/arnold/cycles.py` implements the 7-day grid.** `end_date_for(start, weeks)` is
   `weeks * 7 - 1`; `describe()` counts weeks by `// 7`; `week_type` (`standard|deload`) is
   defined as "a property of a WEEK".

That grid is the strength-training convention. Endurance planning does not share it: the
motivating source (`docs/research/2026-09-28_rossner-aerobic-system-four-intensities.md`)

# After Action Lessons Learned (AALL): ADR-006 Unified Workout Schema

**Document ID:** AALL-006  
**Date:** January 20, 2026  
**Project:** Arnold - AI Fitness Coaching System  
**Subject ADR:** ADR-006: Unified Workout Schema — Segments + Sport-Specific Child Tables  
**Status of Subject ADR:** Superseded by ADR-007  
**Lifespan:** January 13, 2026 → January 20, 2026 (7 days in production)

---

## 1. Executive Summary

ADR-006 introduced a segment-based workout schema with sport-specific child tables to handle multi-modal workouts. The design was technically sound but over-engineered for actual use patterns. After one week in production, we rolled back to a simpler three-table model (ADR-007). This AALL documents what went wrong, why, and how to avoid similar mistakes.

**Bottom line:** We solved problems we didn't have while creating problems we didn't anticipate.

---

## 2. Background

### 2.1 Problem Statement (as understood at decision time)

The system needed to handle:
- Multi-modal workouts (CrossFit, brick workouts, hybrid training)
- Sport-specific metrics (SWOLF, power, strokes, splits)
- 35+ years of diverse athletic history
- Decades of future data

### 2.2 Decision Made

Adopt a discriminator pattern:
```
workouts → segments (discriminator: sport_type) → child tables
           ├── strength_sets
           ├── running_intervals
           ├── rowing_intervals
           ├── cycling_intervals
           └── swimming_laps
```

**Date:** 2026-06-27
**Decider:** Brock
**Status:** RULED / final
**Supersedes:** D1 (segment) and D2 (block=mesocycle) in
`docs/ontology/training-domain-vocabulary.md`; and **ADR-013 as written** (which
encoded the segment direction).
**Trigger:** Literature + tooling check (2026-06-27) during TEVV revalidation of
ADR-013, plus OO/polymorphism re-framing by Brock.

---

## What changed and why

ADR-013 (drafted 2026-06-26) ratified D1 = "segment" for the within-workout grouping
and D2 = "block" for the mesocycle. A literature/tooling check run the next day found:

1. **"segment" is not a sport-science term for the within-workout grouping** — it was
   a project coinage chosen to dodge the "block" overload. The field has no single
   generic word; it uses block / superset / circuit / complex.
2. **The dominant coaching tooling (TrainingPeaks) and the clinical-trial literature
   use "block" for exactly the within-workout grouping**, with Single/Superset/Circuit
   as its subtypes — i.e. an abstract container with polymorphic kinds. That is the
   OO model Brock independently arrived at.
3. Therefore "segment" diverged from every external system for no gain; "block" is
   both literature-aligned AND already the physical name (`blocks`, `:PlannedBlock`),
   so adopting it costs ZERO and eliminates the rename pressure D1 created.

# Canonical Exercise Creation & Alias-First Resolution

**Status:** Active convention. Ratified by Brock 2026-06-11.
**Supersedes:** the open questions in `docs/2026-06-07_canonical-exercise-creation-design.md`
(that brief asked the questions; this doc records the answers and the enforced mechanism).
**Implements:** `cc_tasks/2026-06-11_alias-first-resolution-and-canonical-creation.md`.
**Applies to:** `arnold-training-mcp` exercise resolution and creation
(`neo4j_client.py`, `server.py`). ADR-012 (every write reads back its own effect) applies.

---

## The six rulings

1. **Alias-first resolution, fuzzy demoted to suggestion-only.** Lookup order per
   input: **exact name** (normalized, case-insensitive, trimmed) → **exact alias**
   → **fuzzy / description = candidates ONLY**. The system NEVER auto-accepts a
   non-exact match. A wrong fuzzy score can no longer silently corrupt data —
   non-selection is structural, not score-tuned.
2. **Many names, one node.** Common names are explicit aliases on the node. Aliases
   may point into ANY namespace (`CANONICAL:FFDB:*`, `EXERCISE:*`,
   `CANONICAL:ARNOLD:*`) — no node migration.
3. **New canonicals land in `CANONICAL:ARNOLD:` only.** `FFDB` and `EXERCISE`
   namespaces are frozen for additions.
4. **Minimum shape on create:** name + the common name used (as first alias, if it
   differs from the name) + at least one link (`TARGETS` a Muscle OR `INVOLVES` a
   MovementPattern) + provenance (`source`, `created_at`). No orphan n

# Progression policy — how a prescription moves week to week

**Status:** current. Landed 2026-09-01 with
`cc_tasks/2026-09-01_pb-02-block-library-and-progression-policy.md` §B.
**Code:** `src/arnold/workout_write/progression.py`.
**Schema:** `migrations/2026-09-01_block_templates_and_progression.cypher`.

## The one rule

**The default is `maintain`. No policy is not "build".**

An exercise with no `PROGRESSES` edge does not move — not its load, not its
reps, not by any amount, ever. This document exists because the opposite was
happening: face pulls and Kelso shrugs crept up week over week because nothing
declared that they should not. Absence of a declaration is a declaration of
maintenance, and any code that reads a missing policy as "unknown, so progress"
has inverted the contract.

```
(:Person)-[:PROGRESSES {policy, delta_lbs, delta_reps, rep_min, rep_max,
                        updated_at, source, note}]->(:Exercise)

`:Preference.preference_text` is free prose (verified 2026-09-01 in
`src/arnold/knowledge/models.py`); reading a numeric increment back out of prose
at plan time would be an LLM call in the daily path, which the plan-builder
parent task forbids. ADR-010 remains the home for prose preferences. This is a
typed planning parameter, so it gets typed fields.

# Workout Structure Ontology

**Last Updated:** 2026-01-20  
**Status:** Active  
**Supersedes:** ADR-006 (Unified Workout Schema)

> **Vocabulary + columns per ADR-013 (block/cycle, 2026-06-27) and
> `docs/ontology/training-domain-vocabulary.md`.** The within-workout grouping is a
> **block** (physical `blocks` / `:PlannedBlock`) — canonical word == physical name,
> no rename. Training time-spans (meso/micro/macrocycle) are **cycles**

This document defines the canonical data model for workout tracking in the Arnold system. The design prioritizes simplicity over flexibility—we built for the 95% case (strength training) rather than hypothetical future modalities.
